subject: Deployment resource plan and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Lin <jared.lin@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment resource plan and next steps

Hi Jared — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private correctly: 

- Traffic profile: you mentioned a steady-state of ~350 TPS for inference requests during business hours with two short daily spikes to ~900 TPS for batch processing. Please confirm if this is request-per-second or model-invocation TPS.
- Token mix: rough estimate was 60% short prompts (<=256 tokens) and 40% long conversations (avg 1,200 tokens including response).
- Latency SLO: target p95 <= 250ms for interactive paths; batch jobs can tolerate up to 5s.
- Data residency: primary US with an eventual EU workload in H1 2027 — may push Private/VPC needs for sensitive PHI flows.

Attached: traffic-patterns-nov2026.csv (raw logs) and an initial resource-estimate-v1.xlsx that Karthik and I will update.

Key open questions for sizing Dedicated:
- Preferred GPU family? You mentioned familiarity with A40 in-house but open to H100 for quantized 8-bit workloads. Any procurement constraints?
- Concurrency expectations per user/session (avg active concurrent sessions during peak)?
- Typical sequence lengths and how often you expect context-window resets (KV cache reuse).

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik to propose 2 SKU options (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) with expected steady-state and burst capacity.
2) 45-minute sizing workshop next week with your infra and procurement to align on GPU family and procurement timeline.
3) I’ll loop in our Security lead if Private/VPC is prioritized for PHI.

If this aligns, I’ll send calendar options for the workshop and Karthik will drop a first-pass SKU sheet by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

From: Jared Lin <jared.lin@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Deployment resource plan and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 350 TPS number is model invocations (each user action triggers 1 invocation). Spikes to 900 TPS happen for scheduled processing windows (approx 12:00-12:20 and 18:00-18:10) and last ~10-20 min.
- Token counts: for short prompts average is ~120 tokens, long conversations average ~1,200 tokens as you noted. Response size tends to be ~300 tokens on average for the long flows.
- Concurrency: during peak we see ~4,500 concurrent users, but only ~12% are active inference at any instant — that maps to roughly 540 concurrent inference streams at steady state, and up to ~1,400 during spikes.
- KV cache: many sessions reuse context across several invocations (chat-like) — estimate cache hit ~70%.
- Procurement constraints: we can purchase H100s but prefer a mixed approach if it reduces cost. A40s are what we currently have on-prem for other workloads.

Happy to do a sizing workshop. 30 Nov after 2pm PST or 1 Dec morning PT works for our infra folks. Procurement looped on email to help with timing.

-Jared
Jared Lin
Platform Lead, AcmeHealth
jared.lin@acmehealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jared Lin <jared.lin@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment resource plan and next steps

Thanks Jared — very helpful numbers. I sketched two contrasting SKU drafts in the attached spreadsheet: 

Option A (Cost-optimized):
- GPU flavor: A40 / 80GB (mixed precision + 8-bit quantized where safe)
- Steady-state: provisioned pool sized for 400 effective concurrent streams (accounts for 70% cache hit -> lower per-token compute)
- Burst: autoscale to 1,200 concurrent streams for the scheduled windows (uses burst credits)
- Expected p95 latency ~300-500ms for long-context flows; p95 ~160-220ms for short prompts
- Notes: lower monthly cost but risk of higher latency on heavy long-seq workloads

Option B (Latency-optimized):
- GPU flavor: H100 / 80GB (TF32 + quant kernels for low-latency decoding)
- Steady-state: pool sized for 600 concurrent streams
- Burst: autoscale to 1,600 concurrent streams
- Expected p95 latency ~180-240ms for long-context flows; p95 ~120-160ms for short prompts
- Notes: higher cost but better headroom for concurrency and lower tail latency

Sizing notes and assumptions (please review):
- We assume average long-conversation token work is 1,500 tokens total (prompt+response) for cost calc.
- Tokenization overhead and tokenizer differences can add ~5-8% token delta; we can run a quick tokenization sample if you want precise estimates.
- We modeled KV cache hit at 70% which reduces compute significantly; if real hit is <50% that pushes us to Option B.

Open asks to finalize estimates:
1) Confirm whether the spike windows are flexible (can you spread or shift processing?)
2) Can procurement accept a mixed fleet approach (A40 steady + H100 for latency-critical routes)?
3) Any hard constraints on p95 SLO for the interactive product beyond the 250ms target?

I attached resource-estimate-v1.xlsx with per-GPU concurrency assumptions and cost delta. If helpful we can profile a 1-hour sample on your logs with our optimizer to validate KV cache benefits and effective tokens/sec.

If the workshop is agreed, I’ll present a 25-minute slide with cost/latency tradeoffs and a recommended default.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

All — thanks for the quick turn. TL;DR: schedule workshop and validate KV cache hit rate with a short profiling run before we finalize SKU.

Action items we agreed:
- Marissa: send calendar invite for 60-minute workshop (we’ll include our infra, solutions, and procurement); proposed window 1 Dec 09:30–10:30 PT (Jared, you mentioned 1 Dec morning PT works)
- Karthik: finalize the two SKU drafts into slides + attach the resource-estimate-v1.xlsx; include explicit per-token cost and expected monthly run-rate for both steady-state and 2x burst. Due EOD tomorrow (2 Dec).
- Jared / AcmeProcurement: confirm whether mixed fleet is acceptable and share any procurement timelines or vendor-preference constraints.
- Mina: I’ll have Security ready to join if you confirm PHI flows; otherwise we’ll keep the workshop focused on sizing.

Quick notes for the workshop agenda: 1) traffic and tokenization validation (15m), 2) SKU tradeoff and cost model (20m), 3) ops/auto-scale and SLA handoff (15m), 4) procurement questions (10m).

Attachments: resource-estimate-v1.xlsx (Karthik draft), traffic-patterns-nov2026.csv

If that schedule works I’ll send the invite now.
